notes.summary: Finite-state optimization implements short-row span discovery and exact vertex walks without precision-dependent bisection. Its cost depends on numerical state range.
notes.detailedSummary: For integers H≥1 and p, optimize linear objectives over state-selected subsets of the integer l₁ ball X_H using poly(d,H,||p||∞+1) exact operations. Symmetric subsets admit a basis of actual short rows. When an application supplies a feasible point and finite first boundaries, exact parametric comparisons implement at most d rank-increasing steps to a vertex. Integer active systems give integral outputs by determinant scaling, with cofactor height bounds and polynomial intermediate encoding lengths. State-predicate costs must be included when nonconstant.
notes.text:
# Finite-state optimization and exact vertex walks

Fix integers d,H≥1 and p∈Z^d, and write A=||p||∞ and X_H={x∈Z^d:||x||₁≤H}. All algorithms below use exact arithmetic and comparisons, fixed tie rules, and endpoint witnesses. A state predicate is assumed evaluable in constant time, as are all threshold predicates used below. Otherwise its evaluation cost must be charged.

For an objective a∈R^d, let D_j(t) be the minimum aᵀx over endpoints of j signed coordinate moves with pᵀx=t. The recurrence is

  D_0(0)=0,
  D_{j+1}(t)=min_{i∈{1,…,d}, ε∈{−1,1}} [D_j(t−εp_i)+εa_i],  0≤j<H.

Only reachable entries participate. A witness is obtained by adding εe_i to the chosen predecessor. Every such endpoint belongs to X_H, including paths with cancellations, and each x∈X_H occurs at j=||x||₁. Minimizing over j≤H and selected final states therefore optimizes over exactly the corresponding subset of X_H. Maxima use −a. There are at most 2HA+1 states per layer, so the arithmetic count is polynomial in d,H,A+1, independently of a's magnitude or precision.

For a symmetric subset Z selected by states, return an empty basis if Z is empty. Otherwise start with E={0} and maximize hᵀx over Z for an integer basis h of E⊥. A positive maximum supplies a row outside E. If every maximum is zero, symmetry implies that all rows of Z lie in E. Thus at most d rank increases and O(d²) optimizations produce a basis consisting of actual rows of Z.

Here is the exact boundary procedure used in both later constructions. Let Y⊆X_H be state-selected, let β∈{0,1}, and suppose z is feasible for xᵀz≥β, x∈Y. Given a direction v for which feasibility along z+tv is exactly 0≤t≤t* with finite t*, minimize xᵀ(z+tv) symbolically at t=t*+0. Each DP comparison has difference α+γt. For γ=0 its sign is immediate. Otherwise its root is ρ=−α/γ. A negative root lies left of the germ. For ρ≥0, the ordinary DP test min_{x∈Y}xᵀ(z+ρv)≥β decides ρ≤t*, including equality. This determines which side of every root contains the right-hand germ and hence every comparison. If an ordinary DP takes T operations, the symbolic computation takes O(T²) operations up to polynomial witness-handling costs.

Finiteness of Y and t* implies that some negative-slope row is tight at t*. The minimizing row a at the right-hand germ is also tight with aᵀv<0, so

  t*=(β−aᵀz)/(aᵀv).

This includes t*=0 and simultaneous tight rows. No precision-dependent bisection occurs.

To walk with additional fixed equalities, maintain independent active integer rows. Choose a nonzero integer null direction v while their rank is below d. Whenever the application guarantees a finite boundary, the procedure above adds an independent active row: its negative pairing with v excludes membership in the old span. Feasibility and old equalities persist, and at most d steps reach z=R⁻¹b for a nonsingular active-row matrix R. For integer right sides b, |det R|z is integral. Each coordinate is a signed sum of b_j times the cofactors obtained by deleting row j. A determinant is at most the product of its row Euclidean norms, by Gram–Schmidt. This gives the coefficient bounds in the applications without rounding the starting point.

The same construction controls intermediate encoding lengths. If active rows have l₁ norm at most M≥1, minors provide null directions with ||v||∞≤M^(d−1). Every boundary slope has 0<|aᵀv|≤HM^(d−1), and

  z'=(I−vaᵀ/(aᵀv))z+βv/(aᵀv).

There are at most d updates, so the encoding lengths remain polynomial in the initial rational lengths and d,log(H+1),log(M+1). Comparison roots pair z and v with differences of witnesses of norm at most 2H. DP values may be recomputed by pairing their bounded endpoint with the objective, keeping their lengths polynomial as well. Span calculations use minors of short integer rows. None of these arithmetic counts depends on the initial real data's magnitude or precision. Their dependence on the numerical state range HA remains.

notes.summary: A bounded-height promise yields a finite-state encoding of all three signs or a sound failure certificate. A separate vertex walk restores exact zeros with determinant-size coefficients.
notes.detailedSummary: For W∈Z^d and integers H,P≥1, the learner either rules out a sign-equivalent integer vector of height P or returns K=2H² and ||p||∞≤16dP²H³, with positive/negative labels beyond ±3K/2 and zero labels within ±K/2. Its cost is poly(d,H,P). Given integer K≥1 and p with exact label classes pᵀx≥K, |pᵀx|<K, pᵀx≤−K, a second algorithm returns an exact three-sign integer representative of height dH^(d−1) in poly(d,H,||p||∞+1,log(K+1)) operations. Both have polynomial intermediate encoding lengths. Numerical parameter dependence leaves the unrestricted poly(d,log N) operation bound open.
notes.text:
# A bounded statistic and exact zero restoration

Let d,H≥1 be integers and X_H={x∈Z^d:||x||₁≤H}.

For W∈Z^d and integer P≥1, there is a deterministic algorithm that either correctly rules out every v∈Z^d with ||v||∞≤P having W's three signs on X_H, or returns K=2H² and p∈Z^d with ||p||∞≤16dP²H³ and

  Wᵀx>0 ⇒ pᵀx≥3K/2,
  Wᵀx=0 ⇒ |pᵀx|≤K/2,
  Wᵀx<0 ⇒ pᵀx≤−3K/2.

Its arithmetic count is polynomial in d,H,P, independently of W's magnitude. All intermediate encoding lengths are polynomial in the binary input length.

To prove this, put s(x,b)=sgn(2Wᵀx+b), b∈{−1,1}. These signs are nonzero. Start with p=0 and c=p/K. Whenever s(x,b)(cᵀx+b)<1/2, replace p by p+s(x,b)x. An integer height-P representative v, if one exists, satisfies s(x,b)(2vᵀx+b)≥1. Thus each update decreases ||c−2v||₂² by more than

  1/K−H²/K²=1/(4H²).

The initial distance is at most 4dP², so T=16dP²H² updates are impossible under the promise. Reaching T updates certifies failure. Every earlier iterate has height at most TH. At successful termination the two choices of b give the displayed margins.

Violations are found by n1's DP with objective W. At each reachable state t=pᵀx, let m(t),M(t) be the minimum and maximum Wᵀx over all layers. A positive-label violation exists precisely when t/K+b<1/2 and 2M(t)+b>0. A negative-label violation exists precisely when t/K+b>−1/2 and 2m(t)+b<0. The corresponding witness gives the update. Thus the search uses polynomially many bounded-state operations. Its W-dependent values are pairings with short integer witnesses, establishing the stated encoding bound. The statistic encodes all three labels by thresholds ±K, but p itself need not preserve zeros.

More generally, suppose integers K≥1 and p,W∈Z^d satisfy, on X_H,

  Wᵀx>0 ⇔ pᵀx≥K,
  Wᵀx=0 ⇔ |pᵀx|<K,
  Wᵀx<0 ⇔ pᵀx≤−K.

Then an implemented deterministic algorithm returns q∈Z^d with exactly these three signs and ||q||∞≤dH^(d−1). Its arithmetic count is polynomial in d,H,||p||∞+1,log(K+1), independently of W's magnitude, with polynomial intermediate binary lengths.

For W=0 return q=0. Otherwise use n1's symmetric-span procedure on Z={x∈X_H:|pᵀx|<K}, obtaining a short-row basis of E=span Z. Let Y={x∈X_H:pᵀx≥K}. Start at z=W in

  F={z∈E⊥:xᵀz≥1 for all x∈Y}.

Initially activate the basis of E. For each deficient-rank step, choose a nonzero integer null direction v and orient it so cᵀv≤0, where c_i=sgn(W_i). When W_i=0, e_i∈Z, hence v_i=0. Therefore some nonzero-W coordinate has c_i v_i<0. Its row c_i e_i belongs to Y, so the first boundary is finite. Apply n1's walk with β=1 and M=H.

At termination the active system Rz=b has short integer rows and b∈{0,1}^d. Set q=|det R|z. Feasibility gives qᵀx>0 on Y, E⊥ gives zero on Z, and negation handles negative rows. The cofactor formula in n1 gives |q_i|≤dH^(d−1). Its rational-workspace argument applies from z=W. This proof uses the label promise, not the preceding learner, so another source of the same statistic may replace that learner.

Combining the two constructions restores exact zeros after learning. The numerical dependence on H,P, and statistic height prevents a general poly(d,log N) arithmetic bound when H=N−1. The target coefficient size alone does not resolve that remaining algorithmic gap.

notes.summary: Explicit quantization and projection tests yield small objective-positive closed-conformal rays, including horizontal progress. A geometric family rules out universal success of this branch.
notes.detailedSummary: For integers H,B≥1 and L≥H, normalize nonzero w, round to p, and span the short rows with |pᵀx|≤L. The branch succeeds if H||proj_E a||∞<(L+1−H/2)/B and hᵀ(a−proj_E a)>0, returning integer u closed-conformal with w, hᵀu>0, and ||u||∞≤H^(d−1). Work is poly(d,H,B), with intermediate encoding lengths polynomial in input length. Only H≤L<B can succeed. Unit-anchor inputs with ||W||∞>2B yield horizontal rays and an objective can certify escape from a given span. At H=4, w_i=(5/2)^i defeats every polynomial quantization budget, although it has an O(d)-bit exact representative. The general arithmetic-operation target remains open.
notes.text:
# Guarded conformal rays and a limitation of quantization

Let d,H,B≥1 and L≥H be integers, and let w,h∈R^d. On X_H={x∈Z^d:||x||₁≤H}, call u closed-conformal with w if wᵀx=0 implies uᵀx=0 and wᵀx≠0 implies sgn(wᵀx)uᵀx≥0. The following deterministic branch either fails its stated tests or returns such a u∈Z^d with

  hᵀu>0,  ||u||∞≤H^(d−1).

Its arithmetic count is polynomial in d,H,B, independently of w,h's magnitudes and precision. Rational intermediate lengths are polynomial in the total encoded input length. Closed conformity allows additional zeros and is weaker than exact three-sign preservation.

For w=0 report failure. Otherwise put a=w/||w||∞ and round Ba to a nearest integer vector p with fixed ties. Binary search on [−B,B] implements rounding. Then ||p||∞≤B and ||a−p/B||∞≤1/(2B). Use n1's symmetric-span algorithm on

  Z_L={x∈X_H:|pᵀx|≤L}

to find a basis of E=span Z_L consisting of actual short rows. Compute r=proj_E a and q=a−r by rational linear algebra on that basis. Require

  H||r||∞<(L+1−H/2)/B,  hᵀq>0.

Every original zero row lies in E, since |pᵀx|≤H/2 for such a row. For x∈X_H outside E, integrality gives |pᵀx|≥L+1, and

  sgn(pᵀx)qᵀx≥(L+1−H/2)/B−H||r||∞>0.

The estimate without the projection term identifies sgn(wᵀx)=sgn(pᵀx). Thus q has the required strict signs outside E and annihilates E.

Let Y={x∈X_H:pᵀx≥L+1} and C={z∈E⊥:xᵀz≥0 for x∈Y}. Every point of C is closed-conformal with w, by the preceding sign identification and symmetry. Put c_i=sgn(q_i). If q_i=0 then e_i∈E, since otherwise the displayed strict inequality would contradict q_i=0. If q_i≠0 then e_i∉E and c_i e_i∈Y. These coordinate constraints imply cᵀz=||z||₁ on C. Consequently the section C∩{cᵀz=1} is bounded and contains z_0=q/(cᵀq), with hᵀz_0>0.

Apply n1's walk to this section, with β=0. Initially activate the basis of E and cᵀz=1. At each step orient the integer null direction v so hᵀv≥0. Since cᵀv=0 and v vanishes on the fixed zero coordinates, some oriented coordinate constraint has negative slope. Thus each first boundary is finite, while the objective stays positive. The walk uses only the finite-state DP on Y, including at zero-length steps.

At its endpoint take R with c as first row. The other active rows are homogeneous and have l₁ norm at most H, and the right side is e_1. Return u=|det R|R⁻¹e_1. It belongs to C, is integral, and has hᵀu>0. Only cofactors deleting c occur, so n1's determinant bound gives ||u||∞≤H^(d−1). The possibly dense row c does not affect this final height bound. For intermediate lengths use n1 with M=max(H,d), starting from the rational projection and normalization when inputs are rational. State ranges are bounded by HB, and h is used only in exact objective tests and orientations.

If L≥B then E=R^d and the objective test fails. Only L=H,…,B−1 need be tried, so threshold enumeration is polynomial in B. This is a poly(d,log N) branch only with both B and H polynomially bounded in those parameters. It supplies no universal success or termination guarantee.

For the horizontal application, use dimension d+1 and V=(W,1) with ||W||∞>2B. The normalized anchor rounds to zero, putting its coordinate row in E and forcing every output's anchor to vanish. With objective h=(W−proj_F W,0), where F is a given ordinary-coordinate span, success implies that the ordinary part lies outside F. Such a horizontal ray is progress, not a final representative.

The branch fails on a concrete family even when H=4. Let w_i=(5/2)^i for i=0,…,d−1. Coordinate rows and the positive rows e_{i+1}−2e_i and 3e_i−e_{i+1} force every closed-conformal integer u to satisfy

  u_i≥0,  2u_i≤u_{i+1}≤3u_i.

If u is nonzero then u_0≥1 and u_{d−1}≥2^(d−1). After normalization a_0=(2/5)^(d−1). Whenever Ba_0<1/2, rounding gives p_0=0, so e_0 belongs to every Z_L and every output must instead have u_0=0. Thus for each polynomial B(d), every threshold fails for all sufficiently large d. This excludes universal success of this quantized-hull branch. It does not exclude the desired sign-compression theorem: clearing denominators gives the exact integer representative 2^(d−1)w with O(d)-bit coefficients. The unrestricted poly(d,log N) construction remains unresolved.
